chunks.title: Image Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). Overview.
description: Text-to-image and image-to-image generation with 72 T2I models and 74 I2I models, supporting multi-image reference input and inpainting.
shortDescription: Generate images from text prompts or transform existing images using 72 text-to-image and 74 image-to-image models, with support for multi-image reference input and inpainting.
fullDescription: Image Studio is SmartVideo GO's primary image generation workspace. It offers text-to-image generation across 72 models and image-to-image generation across 74 models, including popular options like Flux, Nano Banana, and Google models. Upload up to 14 reference images for I2I mode, apply inpainting to specific regions, and control aspect ratio, resolution, quality, seed, and strength. Models expose schema-driven options for aspect ratio, resolution, quality, and effects, so the available controls adapt automatically to your selected model.
bestFor: Creative teams, marketers, designers, and content creators who need versatile image generation or image-to-image transformation with extensive model choice and fine-grained control.
whenToUse:
- Creating original images from text descriptions
- Transforming existing images with style or content changes
- Inpainting specific regions of an image
- Generating multiple variations with seed control
whenToUseAnother:

chunks.title: Image Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). Overview.
- Use Video Studio when you need video output instead of still images
- Use Cinema Studio when you want director-grade cinematic stills with camera controls
- Use Thumbnail Studio when creating YouTube thumbnails optimized for click-through rate
- Use Layers Studio when you need to decompose images into layers, upscale, or remove backgrounds
businessValue: Image Studio removes the traditional barriers between concept and finished visual. Where a photoshoot or freelance designer once required days of scheduling and hundreds of dollars, Image Studio produces draft visuals in minutes and refined outputs in a single session. Teams running multi-channel campaigns can generate dozens of image variants to test messaging, colorways, and composition without commissioning additional rounds of creative work.
The cost advantage is significant for high-volume use cases. E-commerce managers can generate product-on-background shots, lifestyle mockups, and banner variants without a studio setup or photo editing skills. Marketing teams running A/B tests can produce multiple headline-and-image combinations in the time it would take to brief a single designer. The 72 T2I and 74 I2I models mean the studio adapts to many visual styles, reducing the need to switch between specialized tools.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). Overview.
Quality is no longer gated behind software expertise. Inpainting lets teams fix individual elements without regenerating an entire image, and multi-image reference input lets designers steer composition with visual precedent rather than words alone. Seed control supports brand consistency across campaigns, while schema-driven options ensure each model's controls are relevant rather than overwhelming.

chunks.title: Image Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). How to use.
howToUse: Enter a text prompt or upload reference images, select a model and aspect ratio, then generate. For I2I, upload one or more reference images and adjust strength.
howToSteps:
- Type a text prompt describing the image you want, or upload one or more reference images for I2I mode.
- Select a generation mode: text-to-image, image-to-image, or inpainting.
- Choose a model from the available T2I or I2I catalog.
- Set aspect ratio, resolution, and quality to match your deliverable.
- For I2I, adjust the strength slider to control how much the output resembles your reference.
- Optionally set a seed for reproducible results.
- Click Generate and wait for the model to produce your image.
gettingStarted:
- Open Image Studio from the studio list and confirm your MuAPI key is configured in Settings.
- Select a generation mode: Text-to-Image for new visuals or Image-to-Image to transform an existing image.
- Type a text prompt describing your desired image, including subject, style, lighting, and composition details.
- Choose a model from the T2I or I2I catalog depending on your mode.
- Set aspect ratio, resolution, and quality to match your deliverable requirements.
- For I2I mode, upload one or more reference images and adjust the strength slider to control resemblance.
- Optionally set a seed for reproducible results, then click Generate.

chunks.title: Image Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). How to use.
- Review the output, iterate on the prompt or model, and download when satisfied.
tips:
- Be specific in prompts: include subject, style, lighting, and composition for more predictable results.
- Upload multiple reference images in I2I mode to blend styles or subjects.
- Lock the seed after getting a good result to create variations.
- Check model schemas for available aspect ratios and effects.
- Use negative prompts or tags to exclude unwanted elements from generated images.
bestPractices:
- Be specific in prompts: include subject, style, lighting, and composition for more predictable results.
- Upload multiple reference images in I2I mode to blend styles or subjects rather than relying on a single image.
- Lock the seed after getting a good result to create controlled variations without drifting off-brand.
- Check model schemas for available aspect ratios and effects before committing to a model.
- Use negative prompts or tags to exclude unwanted elements such as watermarks, text artifacts, or specific colors.
- Start with a model known for your target style: Flux for photorealism, Nano Banana for illustration, Google models for structured scenes.
- Use inpainting to fix localized issues instead of regenerating the entire image.
- Batch your generation session by preparing prompts and model selections in advance to reduce switching cost.

Image Studio (/studio/image). Problems and limits.
- question: Why is my generation failing? | answer: Ensure your MuAPI key is valid and you have sufficient balance. Check the troubleshooting steps for specific errors.
- question: What's the difference between T2I and I2I? | answer: T2I (text-to-image) generates new images from text prompts only. I2I (image-to-image) transforms uploaded reference images using AI, preserving composition while changing style or content.
- question: Can I batch-generate multiple images at once? | answer: Image Studio generates one output per request. Use seed variations or generate multiple times to build a set of images.
- question: Which models support inpainting? | answer: Inpainting support varies by model. Check the model schema in the studio UI to see if inpainting options are available for your selected model.
- question: How do I choose the right model? | answer: Review the model explanations in Image Studio. Some models excel at photorealism, others at illustration or stylized art. Test a few to find the best fit for your use case.
- question: Can I use generated images commercially? | answer: Commercial use depends on the specific model's license and your MuAPI plan terms. Check the model documentation and your agreement for usage rights.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: T2I: Text-to-image: generating a new image from a text description only. | I2I: Image-to-image: transforming an existing image using AI while preserving its core composition. | Inpainting: Regenerating only a selected region of an image, such as fixing a text overlay or swapping a background element. | Strength (I2I): A slider from 0 to 1 controlling how much the output resembles the reference image. Lower values preserve more of the original; higher values allow more creative deviation. | Seed: A numeric value that initializes the random generation process. Using the same seed with the same prompt and model produces reproducible results. | MuAPI: The backend API key that authenticates generation requests. A valid key with sufficient balance is required for all generation. | Flux: A leading image generation model known for photorealism and prompt adherence. | Nano Banana: A model optimized for illustration and stylized art. | Aspect Ratio: The proportional relationship between image width and height, such as 16:9 or 1:1. | Resolution: The pixel dimensions of the output image, such as 1024x1024 or 1920x1080. | Quality Preset: A generation setting that trades speed for detail; higher quality presets typically take longer but produce sharper results.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Studio (/studio/video). Overview.
description: Text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video generation across 90 T2V, 131 I2V, and 36 V2V models with motion control support.
shortDescription: Generate videos from text, images, or existing video using 90 text-to-video, 131 image-to-video, and 36 video-to-video models with motion control support.
fullDescription: Video Studio offers text-to-video generation across 90 models, image-to-video across 131 models, and video-to-video across 36 models including motion control variants. Leading options include Seedance, Kling, Runway, Luma, and MMAudio. Motion control models such as Seedance 2.5 and Kling 2.6/3.0 let you direct camera movement and subject motion with precision. Configure aspect ratio, duration, resolution, and quality, and use reference images or input video to guide the output.
bestFor: Content creators, marketers, social media managers, and video editors who need AI-generated video across a broad model selection with advanced motion control.
whenToUse:
- Creating video clips from text descriptions
- Animating static images into video
- Transforming existing videos with AI
- Applying motion control for precise camera movements
whenToUseAnother:
- Use Image Studio when you need still images instead of video
- Use Lip Sync Studio when you need a portrait or avatar to speak or sing

chunks.title: Video Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Studio (/studio/video). Overview.
- Use Vibe Motion when you want motion graphics like kinetic typography or logo reveals
- Use Recast when you want to swap a character in a video while preserving motion
- Use VFX Studio when you want to apply specific visual effects like levitation or explosions
businessValue: Video Studio compresses video production timelines from weeks to minutes. A typical product demo or brand clip that would require a crew, location, lighting, and post-production can now be generated from a text prompt in under a minute. For teams running multi-platform campaigns, the ability to generate 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1 versions of the same concept from a single prompt eliminates redundant shoots and asset requests.
The cost reduction is equally significant. Replacing a video production sprint with AI-generated clips removes expenses for cameras, crew hours, travel, and editing software seats. Marketing teams can A/B test multiple video concepts before committing to a single direction, and product teams can generate localized variants for different markets without rescheduling shoots. Motion control models like Seedance and Kling add precision that previously required a skilled cinematographer.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Overview

Video Studio (/studio/video). Overview.
Scale benefits come from the model breadth: 90 T2V, 131 I2V, and 36 V2V models mean the studio handles everything from abstract motion graphics to photorealistic character scenes. chunks.text: Glossary: T2V: Text-to-video: generating video from a text description only. | I2V: Image-to-video: animating a static image into a video clip. | V2V: Video-to-video: transforming an existing video while preserving its motion. | Motion Control: Precise control over camera and subject movement, supported by models such as Seedance 2.5 and Kling 2.6/3.0. | Seedance: A motion control model from ByteDance that supports up to 30 reference images and precise camera movements such as orbits and arcs. | Kling: A video generation model known for high-quality output and character fidelity, available in versions 2.6 and 3.0. | Luma: A model optimized for smooth, natural motion in video generation. | Runway: A creative video model known for stylized effects and motion flexibility. | MMAudio: An audio-aware video model that can synchronize generated video with audio inputs. | Duration: The length of the generated video in seconds, limited by model-specific maximums. | Strength (I2V): A control parameter that determines how much the output follows the reference image's composition versus the prompt.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). Overview.
businessValue: Audio Studio compresses audio production from studio bookings and talent fees into a single browser session. A 30-second voiceover that would normally require a voice actor, studio time, and audio editing can be generated in minutes. Podcasters can produce consistent intro music and episode beds without subscribing to a stock music library or hiring a composer. Game developers can prototype sound effects and ambient audio before outsourcing final sound design.
The cost advantage scales with volume. Marketing teams producing multiple campaign variants can generate distinct audio treatments for each without recurring talent fees. Voice persona systems let brands maintain a consistent narrator across hundreds of videos without managing a single contractor's schedule. The built-in audio player eliminates the need to export to a separate tool for review, keeping feedback loops tight.
Quality is accessible without audio engineering skills. Suno's custom mode lets users write exact lyrics and control song structure, while ElevenLabs and Minimax deliver near-human voice synthesis. Negative tags let teams exclude specific instruments or vocal styles without fine-tuning model parameters. Voice cloning from audio samples adds a layer of personalization that was previously available only to large studios with recurring voice talent.

AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Overview.
description: Extracts viral highlight clips and timing markers from long-form videos automatically.
shortDescription: Automatically extract viral highlight clips and timing markers from long-form videos with configurable highlight counts and aspect ratios.
fullDescription: AI Clipping analyzes long-form videos and automatically extracts the most engaging highlight moments. Set how many clips you want and the aspect ratio, and the service returns clip packages with precise timing markers. Use coordinate-only mode if you want to process the clips with your own tools. The service is designed for hook-first framing and caption-ready outputs.
bestFor: Social media managers, content creators, and marketers who need to repurpose long-form video into short-form clips efficiently.
whenToUse:
- Extracting highlights from long-form videos
- Creating short clips from podcasts or interviews
- Generating timing markers for video editing
- Preparing content for social media platforms
whenToUseAnother:
- Use Video Studio when you need to generate new video content
- Use Marketing Studio when you want to turn highlights into polished video ads
- Use Social Publishing when you are ready to publish the extracted clips

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Overview
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Overview.
businessValue: AI Clipping eliminates the manual review phase that consumes hours of editor or producer time. A 60-minute webinar or podcast episode that once required watching end-to-end, marking timestamps, and exporting clips can now be processed in minutes. The service returns timing markers alongside rendered clips, so producers can verify the AI's choices and fine-tune in their editing tool without re-watching the full source.
For social media teams, the batch-ready output means a single long-form piece of content can become a week's worth of short-form clips. Coordinate-only mode lets teams integrate the timing data into existing editing pipelines without changing their workflow. Configurable highlight counts mean one podcast episode can yield three clips for TikTok, five for Instagram Reels, and two for YouTube Shorts without reprocessing the source.
The hook-first framing and caption-ready outputs align with platform best practices. Clips are designed to start with attention-grabbing moments rather than slow introductions, which improves viewer retention and share rates. For agencies managing multiple client accounts, this means more content output per client without increasing headcount.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — How to use
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). How to use.
howToUse: Paste or upload a long-form video URL, set the number of highlights and aspect ratio, then generate. The service returns clip packages with timing markers.
howToSteps:
- Paste or upload a publicly accessible long-form video URL.
- Set the number of highlights you want to extract.
- Choose an aspect ratio for the output clips.
- Optionally enable coordinate-only mode if you want timing data without rendered clips.
- Click Generate and wait for the service to analyze the video and return clip packages.
gettingStarted:
- Open AI Clipping from the studio list and confirm your MuAPI key is configured in Settings.
- Paste or upload a publicly accessible long-form video URL.
- Set the number of highlights you want to extract based on your target platforms.
- Choose an aspect ratio for the output clips, such as 9:16 for TikTok or 16:9 for YouTube Shorts.
- Optionally enable coordinate-only mode if you only need timing data for external editing.
- Click Generate and wait for the service to analyze the video and return clip packages.
- Review the extracted highlights and timing markers.
- Download clips individually or as a package, or send them to another studio for further processing.
tips:
- Use videos with dynamic content for better highlight detection.
- Match aspect ratio to target platform before generating.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — How to use
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). How to use.
- Use coordinate-only mode for integration with external editing tools.
- Review clips and adjust highlight count if needed.
- Pre-trim very long videos into segments under 30 minutes for faster and more accurate clipping.
bestPractices:
- Use videos with dynamic content such as interviews, panel discussions, or presentations for the best highlight detection.
- Pre-trim very long videos into segments under 30 minutes for faster and more accurate clipping.
- Match aspect ratio to the target platform before generating to avoid post-processing resizing.
- Use coordinate-only mode when integrating with external editing tools like Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.
- Request a slightly higher highlight count than you need, then curate manually for quality control.
- Test with different highlight counts to find the sweet spot between coverage and signal-to-noise ratio.
- Use hook-first framing to ensure clips start with engaging moments rather than slow introductions.
- Review clips for context gaps before publishing; AI may miss narrative setup that human editors would preserve.

chunks.title: Vibe Motion — Overview
chunks.text:
Vibe Motion (/studio/vibe-motion). Overview.
businessValue: Vibe Motion replaces the need for After Effects or Cinema 4D expertise for many common motion graphics tasks. A social media manager who needs a kinetic typography clip or a logo reveal can generate it from a sentence rather than learning keyframing or outsourcing to a motion designer. The edit mode lets teams remix existing motion graphics by request ID, turning one good output into a family of variants without starting over.
The time savings compound for recurring content needs. A SaaS company running a weekly product update can generate a consistent motion template, then remix it with new text and data each week instead of rebuilding from scratch. Native audio support via skills recipe means motion graphics can be synchronized to voiceovers or music beds from Audio Studio without manual timeline alignment.
Quality is accessible without software fluency. The studio handles motion pacing, easing, and composition from text descriptions, so teams can focus on messaging rather than technical execution. For brands producing high-frequency social content, this means a consistent motion identity without a dedicated motion graphics budget.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Lip Sync Studio (/studio/lipsync). Overview.
businessValue: Lip Sync Studio removes the recording barrier from video production. A founder who wants to record a product tutorial no longer needs a camera setup, lighting, or multiple takes to get clean audio sync. A marketing team can localize a campaign video for new markets by swapping the audio track and regenerating lip sync without reshooting. An e-learning developer can produce consistent narrator videos from a single portrait image and a script.
The cost and time savings are substantial for high-volume use cases. A training video series that would require a studio day, talent fees, and editing hours can be produced with a single portrait image and pre-written script. Avatar modes let brands maintain a consistent on-camera presence across hundreds of videos without managing talent availability or scheduling conflicts.
Quality is controlled through resolution selection and model choice. Resolution options from 480p to 1080p let teams match output to platform requirements, and 14 models including Infinite Talk, Wan 2.2, and Kling avatars cover both photorealistic and stylized talking-head styles. Video-based lipsync modes support dubbing workflows, and cross-studio handoff from Storyboard streamlines pre-production to production.

howToUse: Upload a portrait image, video, or select an avatar model, upload or provide an audio file, then generate. The output is a talking video synced to the audio.
howToSteps:
- Select a lipsync mode: image-based, video-based, or avatar.

- Upload or provide an audio file or URL.

gettingStarted:
- Open Lip Sync Studio from the studio list and confirm your MuAPI key is configured in Settings.
- Select a lipsync mode: image-based for portrait plus audio, video-based for existing video plus audio, or avatar for Kling avatar generation.
- Upload a portrait image or input video as required by your chosen mode.
- Upload or provide an audio file or URL for synchronization.
- Select a model and resolution appropriate for your use case.
- Optionally enter a text prompt for additional generation guidance.
- Click Generate to create the talking video.
- Download the output or send it to another studio for further processing.
tips:
- Use clear, front-facing portrait images for best results.
- Ensure audio is clear and well-recorded for accurate sync.
- Match resolution to your delivery platform.
- Use seed control for consistent character appearance.
- Use portrait images with even, frontal lighting for the most accurate lip sync.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Lip Sync Studio (/studio/lipsync). How to use.
- Use clear, front-facing portrait images with even, frontal lighting for the most accurate lip sync.
- Ensure audio is clear, well-recorded, and free of background noise for reliable synchronization.
- Use Infinite Talk or Wan 2.2 for general-purpose portrait lipsync; use Kling avatars for consistent character generation.
- Match resolution to your delivery platform: 720p for social media, 1080p for web and presentation.
- Use video-based lipsync mode for dubbing existing content rather than regenerating from scratch.
- Use seed control for consistent character appearance across multiple video generations.
- Test with short audio clips first to validate the model and portrait before committing to longer content.
- Use portrait images with minimal occlusion and neutral expressions for the most reliable sync.

- question: Can I change the voice in an existing video? | answer: Yes, use video-based lipsync mode to sync new audio to an existing video, effectively changing the voice.
- question: What makes a good portrait image for lipsync? | answer: Use a clear, front-facing portrait with good lighting and minimal occlusion. Avoid profiles, extreme angles, or heavily obscured faces.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (/studio/cinema). Overview.
businessValue: Cinema Studio brings director-grade camera controls to AI image generation, collapsing the gap between concept and cinematic still. A product photographer who once needed a $50,000 camera kit, a studio, and a lighting crew can now specify an 8K digital camera with an anamorphic lens at f/1.4 and generate a hero product shot in minutes. A concept artist blocking a film scene can iterate on focal length, camera body, and aperture without scheduling a shoot or waiting for a location scout.
The business value is in iteration speed and creative control. Teams can test 10 camera-and-lens combinations for a single product shot in the time it would take to reconfigure a physical studio. The 6 camera body presets, 11 lens options, 6 focal lengths, and 3 aperture settings map directly to cinematography vocabulary, so directors and DPs can communicate visual intent without translation.
Quality improvements come from the depth-of-field control and cinematic prompt injection. Wide apertures at f/1.4 produce natural bokeh, and 70mm film presets add grain and color response that generic image generators cannot replicate. For brands whose differentiation depends on visual craft, this precision creates a competitive advantage over competitors using generic AI imagery.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (/studio/cinema). How to use.
- Always specify lighting in prompts—'golden hour', 'neon lit', 'high key'—for more cinematic results.
bestPractices:
- Always specify lighting in prompts: golden hour, neon lit, high key, or low key for more cinematic results.
- Combine camera body, lens, and aperture selections for realistic depth of field: anamorphic at f/1.4 produces the most cinematic bokeh.
- Use 70mm film preset for classic anamorphic grain and color response.
- Try different focal lengths to change perspective: 85mm for flattering compression, 35mm for natural perspective, 8mm for extreme wide.
- Include a strong light source in the prompt to trigger lens flares when using anamorphic lenses.
- Lock the seed after getting a preferred result to create controlled variations.
- Use aspect ratios such as 2.39:1 for widescreen cinematic look or 1.85:1 for flat widescreen.
- Start with a detailed scene description and let the camera controls refine the cinematic quality.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (/studio/cinema). Problems and limits.
- question: What camera bodies are available? | answer: 6 camera body presets including 8K digital, 70mm film, 16mm film, and others. Each maps to specific prompt modifiers for cinematic look.
- question: How do lens choices affect the output? | answer: Anamorphic lenses produce wide-aspect cinematic flares. Macro lenses create extreme close-ups with shallow depth. Prime lenses offer classic sharpness.
- question: Can I combine Cinema Studio with other studios? | answer: Yes, send Cinema Studio outputs to Image Studio for further editing, or to Storyboard for scene planning.
- question: What aspect ratios work best for cinema? | answer: 2.39:1 (anamorphic widescreen) and 1.85:1 (flat widescreen) are common cinematic ratios. Check available options in the studio UI.
- question: Can I generate cinematic videos? | answer: No, Cinema Studio generates still images only. Use Video Studio for cinematic video generation with motion control.
- question: How does aperture affect the output? | answer: Wide apertures like f/1.4 create shallow depth of field with blurred backgrounds. Narrow apertures like f/11 keep more of the scene in focus.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Camera Body: A virtual camera preset that maps to specific prompt modifiers for cinematic look, including 8K digital, 70mm film, 16mm film, and others. | Lens: A virtual lens preset that controls perspective, distortion, and depth characteristics, including anamorphic, macro, prime, and others. | Focal Length: The distance between the lens and the image sensor, measured in millimeters, controlling field of view and perspective compression. | Aperture: The opening of the lens diaphragm, measured in f-stops such as f/1.4, f/4, and f/11, controlling depth of field. | Depth of Field: The range of distance in an image that appears acceptably sharp. Wide apertures such as f/1.4 produce shallow depth of field with blurred backgrounds. | Anamorphic Lens: A lens that produces a widescreen cinematic image with characteristic horizontal lens flares and oval bokeh. | 70mm Film: A film format known for high resolution, fine grain, and a distinctive cinematic color response. | Bokeh: The aesthetic quality of the blurred areas in an image, produced by shallow depth of field. | Cinematic Prompt Injection: The process of mapping camera, lens, and lighting selections to prompt modifiers that guide the model toward cinematic aesthetics. | Golden Hour: The period shortly after sunrise or before sunset when light is warm, soft, and directional, favored in cinematography.

chunks.title: Storyboard — Overview
chunks.text:
Storyboard (/studio/storyboard). Overview.
businessValue: Storyboard Studio transforms the pre-production process from a manual, time-consuming task into a structured AI-assisted workflow. A video producer planning a 10-scene marketing video traditionally spends hours writing shot descriptions, planning camera angles, and coordinating character continuity. Storyboard Studio generates scene-by-scene plans with AI-generated shot descriptions, camera/angle controls, and character continuity management in minutes.
The multi-scene planner lets teams build complete video narratives before filming or generating, reducing costly reshoots and rework. For teams working across Storyboard, Video Studio, and other SmartVideo GO studios, the cross-studio handoff means a storyboard plan can flow directly into video generation without re-entering context. Character continuity management ensures that characters maintain consistent appearance across scenes, a critical requirement for branded content and narrative video.
For agencies and production teams managing multiple projects, the episode planner supports serialized content structures. A course creator building an educational video series or a brand building a multi-part campaign can plan the full narrative arc before generating individual scenes.

chunks.title: Storyboard — How to use
chunks.text:
Storyboard (/studio/storyboard). How to use.
howToUse: Create a project with a name and creative brief, add characters with traits and reference images, create episodes, then generate shots with AI. Use the shot editor to arrange scenes and apply camera controls.
howToSteps:
- Open Storyboard and create a new project with a name and creative brief.
- Add characters with names, traits, outfits, and reference images.
- Create episodes with titles and summaries to organize your work.
- Add shots with scene descriptions in the shot editor.
- Apply camera controls to each shot: shot type, angle, movement, camera, lens, focal length, and aperture.
- Generate AI frames for each shot using the model selector.
- Drag and drop shots to reorder the sequence.
- View scene analysis for project statistics and progress.
gettingStarted:
- Open Storyboard Studio from the studio list and confirm your MuAPI key is configured in Settings.
- Create a new storyboard project and enter a project name.
- Add scenes to the storyboard using the scene planner.
- Configure characters for continuity management across scenes.
- Add shot descriptions for each scene, specifying camera angle and movement.
- Review the AI-generated shot suggestions and camera/angle controls.
- Use the episode planner if creating a multi-episode series.
- Export or hand off the storyboard to Video Studio or Cinema Studio for generation.

bestPractices:
- Plan the full narrative arc before adding scenes to ensure coherent pacing and story structure.
- Use the character continuity manager to define character appearance once and maintain consistency across all scenes.
- Leverage camera/angle controls to specify shots intentionally rather than relying on default framing.
- Use the episode planner for serialized content to maintain narrative continuity across episodes.
- Review AI-generated shot suggestions critically: they accelerate planning but require human oversight for creative intent.
- Keep scene descriptions specific and visual to get the best AI-generated shot results.
- Use cross-studio handoff to send storyboard context directly to Video Studio, avoiding re-entry of scene details.
- Export storyboard references for team review and approval before moving to production.

chunks.title: Marketing Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Marketing Studio (/studio/marketing). Overview.
businessValue: Marketing Studio specializes in generating high-converting video ads with selectable avatars, templates, and product images. A direct-to-consumer brand launching a new product can generate a polished marketing video in minutes rather than commissioning a production agency for a 4-6 week turnaround. The template library accelerates production by providing pre-built structures for common ad formats, while selectable avatars let brands choose presenters that match their target demographic.
For brands running multi-platform campaigns, the studio produces video assets optimized for different platforms: short-form vertical videos for TikTok and Reels, square videos for Instagram feed, and horizontal videos for YouTube and Facebook. Product image support lets teams incorporate actual product visuals directly into generated ads, maintaining brand accuracy.
The cost and speed advantages are significant. A professional video production for a 60-second ad costs $5,000-$50,000 depending on talent and production value; Marketing Studio produces similar assets for the cost of API usage. For brands testing multiple creative variations, the ability to generate and iterate quickly enables data-driven creative optimization that is cost-prohibitive with traditional production.

chunks.title: Body Swap — Overview
chunks.text:
Body Swap (/studio/recast). Overview.
businessValue: Recast (Body Swap) Studio enables filmmakers and content creators to swap characters in existing video footage while preserving the original motion, facial expressions, and lighting. A filmmaker who has shot a scene with an actor who is no longer available can replace that actor with a new performer while maintaining seamless motion continuity. This is particularly valuable for long-form content, branded series, and training videos where re-shooting is expensive or impossible.
The underlying Kling and Runway recast technology preserves the original performance's timing, emotion, and body language while mapping a new face and body onto the motion. For brands that need to update spokesperson videos or training content without re-filming, Recast provides a scalable alternative to production.
For social media and comedy creators, the studio enables viral content formats such as celebrity mimicry, face swaps with friends, and personalized videos that drive engagement. The cost and time savings over re-filming are substantial: a single day of re-filming with a professional actor can cost $5,000-$50,000, while Recast produces a replacement in minutes.

- Upload or select the replacement character image or video.

- Preview the swap result to check motion continuity and visual quality.

- Ensure source video has clear, consistent motion.
- Add prompts to guide the character's appearance and style.
- Try different recast models for varying quality and speed.

chunks.title: Body Swap — How to use
chunks.text:
Body Swap (/studio/recast). How to use.
- Use high-contrast, front-facing reference images with plain backgrounds for the most accurate character swaps.
bestPractices:
- Use source footage with clear, well-lit subject separation for best swap results.
- Provide high-quality reference images of the replacement character with consistent lighting and angle.
- Preview swaps before finalizing to catch motion artifacts or edge blending issues.
- Use face-only swap mode for talking head content and full body swap for action or full-body scenes.
- Keep the original motion simple and stable for best swap results; complex motion with occlusion is more challenging.
- Iterate with different blending modes to find the best visual match for your footage.
- For branded content, ensure the replacement character matches brand guidelines for appearance and style.
- Use Recast for content updates rather than re-filming when the original production cost is high.

- question: What makes a good character image? | answer: Use a clear, front-facing photo of the character with good lighting and minimal occlusion. Avoid group photos or heavily stylized images.
- question: Why is my motion not preserved? | answer: Ensure the source video has clear, consistent motion. Very static videos or videos with rapid cuts may not preserve motion well.
- question: How long can the source video be? | answer: Source video duration depends on the recast model. Check model specifications for maximum supported lengths.
- question: Can I control the new character's pose? | answer: Character orientation control is available for precise positioning. Full pose control depends on the model's capabilities.
- question: What video formats are supported for input? | answer: Common video formats are supported. Ensure the source video is accessible via URL and in a format the backend can process.
- question: Can I swap multiple characters in one video? | answer: Recast processes one character swap at a time. For multiple characters, process each swap separately or use Video Studio for full scene generation.
- question: Does Recast preserve the original audio? | answer: Yes, Recast preserves the original motion and audio from the source video while replacing the character.

chunks.title: Layers Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Layers Studio (/studio/layers). Overview.
businessValue: Layers Studio provides image compositing and manipulation capabilities that are essential for professional design workflows. A graphic designer decomposing an image into layers can edit individual elements, replace backgrounds, or blend multiple images into a single composition. The layer decomposition feature extracts foreground, midground, and background elements automatically, saving hours of manual masking work.
Background removal and image expansion are particularly valuable for e-commerce and product photography. A product photographer who needs to remove a busy background for a clean product shot can do so in seconds rather than spending 15-30 minutes on manual masking in Photoshop. Image expansion lets designers extend image boundaries for wider aspect ratios or print layouts without cropping.
Upscaling and image-to-image generation complete the toolkit. A designer who needs to enlarge a low-resolution asset for a print layout can upscale with AI detail reconstruction. Image-to-image generation lets designers transform a sketch or reference into a finished asset while maintaining compositional structure.

chunks.title: Layers Studio — How to use
chunks.text:

howToUse: Upload an image, then choose to decompose into layers, upscale, remove background, expand, or apply I2I transformations. Use drawing tools to annotate before processing.
howToSteps:
- Upload a source image.
- Choose a mode: decompose, upscale, remove background, expand, or I2I.
- For upscaling, select the upscale factor.
- For I2I or decomposition, enter a prompt.
- Use drawing tools to annotate if needed.
- Click Process to apply the transformation.
gettingStarted:
- Open Layers Studio from the studio list and confirm your MuAPI key is configured in Settings.
- Upload the source image to decompose or manipulate.
- Choose a tool: decompose into layers, remove background, upscale, expand, or image-to-image.
- Configure tool-specific settings: layer sensitivity, expansion direction, upscale factor, etc.
- Preview the result and adjust settings if needed.
- Download the processed image or send it to another studio for further work.
- Use layer controls to composite multiple images if needed.
- Export the final asset for use in design or marketing workflows.
tips:
- Use drawing tools to annotate areas before decomposition or upscaling.
- Try different upscale models for varying quality and speed.
- Remove backgrounds before expanding for cleaner outpainting results.
- Use I2I mode for creative transformations after layer work.

chunks.title: Layers Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Layers Studio (/studio/layers). How to use.
- Remove backgrounds before expanding for cleaner outpainting results with fewer artifacts.
bestPractices:
- Use decomposition to separate foreground and background for clean composites rather than manual masking.
- Remove backgrounds before upscaling to reduce noise and artifacts in the upscaled result.
- Use expansion sparingly: large expansions can introduce artifacts; moderate expansions produce better results.
- For image-to-image, provide clear reference images with the desired composition and style.
- Preview all results before downloading to catch artifacts, edge issues, or quality problems.
- Use layer controls to organize complex composites with named layers for easier editing.
- Export assets in high resolution when preparing for print or large-format use.
- Send processed images to Marketing Studio or Social Publishing rather than re-uploading from external tools.

chunks.text:
Workflows (/studio/workflows). Overview.
businessValue: Workflows Studio enables teams to build and automate multi-step AI pipelines that orchestrate multiple SmartVideo GO studios and external services. A marketing operations team that needs to generate 100 video variants with different scripts, avatars, and thumbnails can build a single workflow that sequences Video Studio, Thumbnail Studio, and Social Publishing into an automated pipeline. Instead of manually generating each variant, the workflow runs unattended and produces a complete content package for each variant.
The node-based, drag-and-drop builder makes automation accessible to non-technical users while remaining powerful enough for engineering teams. Templates and community workflows provide starting points for common automation patterns, reducing the time to build production-ready pipelines. The playground lets teams test workflows before deploying them at scale, and API execution enables integration with external systems.
For engineering teams, the API execution layer lets them trigger workflows from external systems, schedule recurring content production, and integrate SmartVideo GO into existing automation frameworks. The cost and time savings over manual execution are substantial: a workflow that replaces 10 hours of manual work per week pays for itself in reduced labor costs.

chunks.title: Agents — Overview
chunks.text:
Agents (/studio/agents). Overview.
businessValue: Agents Studio provides access to template and user-created AI agents that can perform complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. An AI engineer building a customer support agent can configure it to retrieve knowledge, reason about customer issues, and execute actions such as generating support responses or updating records. A marketing operations team can configure an agent to monitor content performance, generate insights, and adjust publishing schedules automatically.
The agent gallery lets users browse pre-built templates for common use cases: support agents, research agents, content generation agents, and analysis agents. Each agent can be customized with specific instructions, knowledge sources, and tools. Conversation history lets teams track agent performance and iterate on prompts and configurations.
For teams building custom agents, the chat interface lets them test agent behavior before deploying to production. The multi-step reasoning capability means agents can break down complex requests into sequential actions, use tools to retrieve data, and synthesize results into actionable outputs. This capability transforms AI from a single-prompt tool into an autonomous assistant that can manage end-to-end workflows.

chunks.title: Design Agent AI — Overview
chunks.text:
Design Agent AI (/studio/design-agent). Overview.
businessValue: Design Agent AI transforms non-designers into capable visual creators through an AI chat interface with 33 built-in templates. A startup founder who needs a logo, social media graphics, and a business card can describe their brand in natural language and receive production-ready designs in minutes rather than hiring a designer for a 2-4 week engagement. The chat-based interface makes design accessible to users with no design software experience.
The 33 built-in templates cover the most common design needs: logos, ads, mockups, posters, social graphics, and more. Each template guides the AI to produce designs appropriate for the use case, reducing the need for design expertise. The autonomous creative capability means the AI can iterate on designs, adjust based on feedback, and produce multiple variations without manual redrawing.
For designers, Design Agent AI accelerates the ideation and iteration process. A designer can generate 10 logo concepts in the time it takes to sketch one, then refine the best concept in design software. The cost advantage over hiring a freelance designer is significant: a freelance designer charges $500-$5,000 for a logo and brand identity; Design Agent AI produces similar assets for the cost of API usage.

howToUse: Select a template or enter a custom design goal in the chat. Go-AI will generate assets (images, videos, audio, text) based on your request. Manage projects and apply brand kits for consistency.
howToSteps:

- Describe your design needs in the chat.
- Attach reference images if needed.
- Apply your brand kit for consistency.
- Review generated assets and use actions to edit, upscale, remove background, or vectorize.
- Save projects to localStorage for later.
gettingStarted:
- Open Design Agent AI from the studio list and confirm your MuAPI key is configured in Settings.
- Start a new chat session in the Design Agent interface.
- Select a design template from the 33 built-in options: logo, ad, mockup, poster, etc.
- Describe your brand, product, or design requirements in natural language.
- Review the AI-generated design and provide feedback for iteration.
- Request variations or adjustments until the design meets your needs.
- Download the final design asset.
- Use the asset in marketing, social media, or brand workflows.
tips:
- Set up a brand kit first for consistent outputs across sessions.
- Use templates as starting points and refine through conversation.
- Upload reference images to guide the assistant.
- Save projects to track iterations and variations.

bestPractices:

- Iterate conversationally: ask for variations, adjustments, and refinements rather than regenerating from scratch.
- Review AI-generated designs critically for brand alignment, readability, and visual hierarchy.
- Download designs in high resolution for print use and web resolution for digital use.
- Use multiple templates to build a cohesive brand identity kit: logo, business card, letterhead, social graphics.
- Save design conversations for reference and future iterations on brand assets.
- Combine AI-generated assets with manual design refinement in design software for production-ready outputs.

- question: Can I use Design Agent AI offline? | answer: No, Design Agent AI requires an internet connection to access the backend API for generation.

- question: What's the difference between agent mode and generate mode? | answer: Agent mode is conversational—you describe needs and Go-AI iterates. Generate mode uses templates for direct asset creation.

- question: Does Design Agent AI support team collaboration? | answer: Projects are stored in localStorage, which is browser-local. For team collaboration, share exported assets manually.

chunks.title: VFX Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
VFX Studio (/studio/vfx-studio). Overview.
businessValue: VFX Studio applies AI-powered visual effects and motion-control camera effects to existing video or image content. A video editor who wants to add a levitation effect to a product video can do so in minutes rather than commissioning a VFX artist for a day of compositing work. The effect library includes Levitate, Explosions, 360 Orbit, and other effects that would traditionally require specialized software and expertise.
Motion-control camera shots simulate professional camera movements such as dolly zooms, crane shots, and orbit moves that would require expensive equipment and skilled operators. A content creator with a static camera setup can add cinematic camera movement to their footage using AI, achieving production values that would otherwise be out of reach.
The studio's ability to apply effects to both video and image content makes it versatile across content types. A product photographer can add a levitation effect to a product image for a social media post, while a video editor can apply the same effect to a product video for a landing page. The cost and speed advantages over traditional VFX are substantial: a single VFX shot from a professional studio can cost $500-$5,000, while VFX Studio produces similar effects for the cost of API usage.

chunks.title: VFX Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
VFX Studio (/studio/vfx-studio). How to use.
howToUse: Select an effect category and specific effect, upload an optional source image, enter a prompt, configure aspect ratio and duration, then generate. Cross-studio handoffs auto-populate prompt and aspect ratio.
howToSteps:
- Select an effect category: AI Effects, Motion Controls, or VFX.
- Choose a specific effect from the category.
- Upload a source image if required by the effect.
- Enter an optional text prompt for guidance.
- Configure aspect ratio, resolution, duration, and quality.
- Click Generate to apply the effect.
gettingStarted:
- Open VFX Studio from the studio list and confirm your MuAPI key is configured in Settings.
- Upload the source video or image to apply effects to.
- Browse the effect library and select an effect: Levitate, Explosion, 360 Orbit, etc.
- Configure effect parameters: intensity, duration, and style.
- Preview the effect on a sample of the footage.
- Adjust parameters if needed and regenerate.
- Export the final video or image with effects applied.
- Share the result or hand off to Social Publishing for distribution.
tips:
- Use clear, high-quality source images for best effects.
- Search and filter effects by category to find the right look.
- Use cross-studio handoff from Storyboard or GO-Viral for seamless workflows.
- Copy prompts from effects and customize for your needs.

chunks.title: VFX Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
VFX Studio (/studio/vfx-studio). How to use.
- Use high-contrast source images with clear subjects for the most impactful effects.
bestPractices:
- Use source footage with clean backgrounds and stable camera work for best effect integration.
- Preview effects on short clips before applying to full videos to catch integration issues early.
- Adjust effect intensity conservatively: strong effects can look artificial if overdone.
- Use motion-control camera effects to add production value to static footage rather than relying on them to fix poorly shot content.
- For product videos, use levitation effects to create eye-catching product showcases without physical rigs.
- For action or dramatic content, use explosion and particle effects to enhance impact.
- Export in the highest quality setting available to preserve effect detail and avoid compression artifacts.
- Combine VFX Studio effects with other SmartVideo GO studios for complete production pipelines.

chunks.title: Thumbnail Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Thumbnail Studio (/studio/thumbnail-studio). Overview.
businessValue: Thumbnail Studio directly impacts the most important metric for video content: click-through rate. A YouTube video with a compelling thumbnail can see CTR improvements from 2 percent to 10 percent or higher, which translates to significantly more views, subscribers, and ad revenue over time. The CTR prompt engine optimizes thumbnail descriptions for engagement by incorporating contrast, emotion, and curiosity elements that drive clicks.
For channels publishing at scale, batch generation with consistent style presets maintains visual branding across dozens or hundreds of videos. The community gallery provides inspiration from trending thumbnails, reducing the guesswork of what designs perform well. A/B testing support lets creators generate multiple thumbnail variants and test them on YouTube to identify the highest-performing design.
The cost advantage over hiring a thumbnail designer is significant. A freelance thumbnail designer charges $20-$100 per thumbnail, which adds up quickly for channels publishing daily or weekly content. Thumbnail Studio produces unlimited thumbnails for the cost of API usage, and the style presets ensure brand consistency without ongoing design direction.

chunks.title: AI Influencer Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
AI Influencer Studio (/studio/ai-influencer). Overview.
businessValue: AI Influencer Studio solves the consistency problem that plagues AI character generation. A social media manager building a virtual influencer or a game developer designing an NPC can define character attributes once and generate a limitless series of portraits that maintain visual continuity. The hierarchical attribute builder with 13 character types, 5 gender options, and 6 ethnicity/origin options lets teams specify diversity and inclusion parameters explicitly rather than hoping for them in freeform generation.
The cost advantage over commissioning character art from illustrators is substantial. A professional character designer charges $500-$5,000 per character depending on complexity; AI Influencer Studio produces infinite variations for the cost of API usage. The nano-banana-pro model's consistency across generations means teams can lock a character design and produce months of content without redrawing.
For brands building virtual ambassadors or influencer campaigns, the studio provides a scalable alternative to human talent contracts. A virtual influencer created in AI Influencer Studio can appear in unlimited posts, videos, and campaigns without scheduling, fees, or exclusivity constraints. CDN-hosted attribute preview images let teams visualize character combinations before generating, reducing iteration cost.

chunks.title: Social Publishing — Overview
chunks.text:
Social Publishing (/studio/social-publishing). Overview.
businessValue: Social Publishing closes the gap between content creation and distribution, turning SmartVideo GO outputs into published social media assets in a single workflow. A social media manager who generates a video in Video Studio and a thumbnail in Thumbnail Studio can publish both to YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok without downloading files, opening platform apps, and re-entering metadata. This eliminates the export-import friction that fragments most content operations workflows.
Per-platform settings ensure each post is optimized for its destination: title, description, and tags for YouTube; caption, placement, and engagement controls for Instagram; caption and privacy for TikTok. Publish history in localStorage provides a single source of truth for what was published, when, and to which platform, reducing duplicate posting and simplifying reporting.
For teams managing multiple accounts per platform, external social account management lets them switch between brand, personal, and client accounts without reauthorizing. The async polling for publish results means the UI stays responsive while the platform processes the upload, and the polling status lets users track progress without refreshing.

chunks.title: GO-Viral — Overview
chunks.text:
GO-Viral (/studio/go-ai-viral). Overview.
businessValue: GO-Viral eliminates the prompt engineering learning curve by providing a continuously refreshed feed of proven AI prompts with attribution. A content creator who struggles to write effective image or video prompts can browse 1,658+ community prompts filtered by model, media type, and category, then copy or hand off the prompt directly to Image Studio or Video Studio. This reduces the trial-and-error cost of prompt discovery from hours to minutes.
The author attribution and source links provide transparency and credit that most prompt aggregators lack, making it easier for teams to understand the context behind a prompt and trace its performance. One-click handoff to other studios eliminates the copy-paste friction between discovery and generation, and the Academy mode provides curated learning content for teams new to AI prompting.
For marketing teams and agencies, the model filter is a practical efficiency tool. Filtering by recommended model such as gptimage, nanobanana, or seedance lets teams find prompts already validated for their preferred backend, reducing failed generations and wasted API calls. The feed's continuous refresh means teams can stay current with trending styles and techniques without manually monitoring social platforms.

chunks.title: Photo Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Photo Studio (/photo-studio). Overview.
businessValue: Photo Studio removes the photoshoot from product photography. An e-commerce manager who needs 20 product images for a catalog update can generate them in a single session without hiring a photographer, renting a studio, or coordinating props and lighting. The 30 style presets across 6 categories provide proven visual treatments for common product types, so users do not need to describe lighting and composition from scratch.
The brand-based generation feature lets teams maintain visual consistency across product lines by selecting a brand context that influences the output style and treatment. Local history filtered by brand lets teams review past generations and reuse successful treatments for new products, reducing the iteration cost of re-briefing a photographer for each shoot.
Cost savings scale with volume. A professional product photoshoot with a photographer, studio, and retoucher can cost $2,000-$10,000 per day and produce 20-50 images. Photo Studio generates the same volume for the cost of API usage, with the added benefit of instant turnaround for seasonal catalog updates, flash sales, and new product launches.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Brand Studio (/brand-studio). Overview.
businessValue: Brand Studio automates the brand research and analysis phase that typically consumes hours of manual website review, competitive analysis, and stakeholder interviews. A marketer analyzing a competitor's brand can paste the competitor's URL and receive a structured brand DNA profile including name, industry, primary colors, and visual characteristics in seconds. For agencies onboarding new clients, this means brand discovery that once took days can happen in a single meeting.
The generated brand DNA feeds directly into downstream studios, ensuring creative assets are aligned with the brand from the first generation. Photo Studio can use the brand context for product photography, Marketing Studio can generate brand-aligned ad creative, and Design Agent AI can apply brand kits consistently across assets. This eliminates the manual handoff of brand guidelines between teams and reduces misalignment between strategy and execution.
For competitive intelligence, the ability to analyze multiple brand URLs in a single session means teams can build competitive landscapes faster. The recent brands list with color previews lets users compare brand palettes side by side, supporting positioning and differentiation strategy. The 8 platform support means brand campaigns can be planned for multiple distribution channels from a single analysis.

### 1. Screenplay & Story Generation
 A good script is cheap; a good story that can actually be filmed by AI is rare.

### 2. Storyboarding & Shot Planning
 A storyboard is the blueprint that stops you from burning credits on random video generations.

### 3. Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts
 Camera movement is the difference between an AI slideshow and a movie.

- Control rendering artifacts using motion strength values and speed sliders.

### 4. Assembling a Short Film
 The film isn't made in the generator; it's made in the editor.
- Cut, trim, and stitch silent video clips to build scene rhythm.
- Set up a multi-layered sound design timeline: voiceover narration, continuous ambient room tone, Foley SFX, and score.

chunks.title: Screenplay & Story Generation
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Screenplay & Story Generation.
# Screenplay & Story Generation
 SmartVideo GO AI Academy — Part of the SmartVideo GO AI course library. Everything in this lesson can be produced end-to-end inside SmartVideo GO AI using its Image, Video, Audio, Cinema, Lip-Sync, Storyboard, VFX, Thumbnail and AI Influencer studios, plus the Create-With-AI recipe system.
 A good script is cheap; a good story that can actually be filmed by AI is rare.
Track: AI Filmmaking
Time: ~40 minutes
Prerequisites: None

chunks.title: Screenplay & Story Generation — The Problem
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Screenplay & Story Generation / The Problem.
Traditional screenplays are written for human actors and camera crews. A standard script might describe "a crowded café with dozens of patrons chatting, as the protagonist slams their coffee cup down in anger, causing coffee to spill onto a passing waiter's uniform."
If you feed a scene like this into a generative AI video model, the rendering will fail completely. The patrons' faces will morph, the physical interaction of spilling coffee on a waiter will look like a surreal glitch, and keeping the protagonist looking like the same person across shots will be impossible.
Most aspiring AI filmmakers start by writing a standard story, only to waste hundreds of generation credits trying to force an AI model to render complex physics, crowds, or constant location shifts. Designing your screenplay with AI-first constraints from day one is the difference between a completed film and a folder of discarded, glitchy clips.

chunks.title: Screenplay & Story Generation — The Concept
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Screenplay & Story Generation / The Concept.
AI-first screenwriting is the process of drafting stories designed specifically around the limitations and strengths of generative models.
### Core Constraints of Generative Video Models:
 The Physics Gap: AI models struggle with complex object interaction (e.g., tying shoes, pouring liquids, buttoning a shirt, eating food).
 The Crowd Dilemma: Any scene with more than two characters in frame dramatically increases visual morphing and reduces identity consistency.
 Continuous Action Limits: Most models generate clips in 4–5 second increments. Long, continuous single-take action scenes are not yet feasible.
To design around these constraints, we write scripts that focus on static character postures, environmental moods, atmospheric lighting, and high-impact dialogue/voiceover rather than complex physical action.
Story Outline → Constraint Check → Visual Script Formatting → Prompts Generation
Instead of describing physical struggle, describe the emotional reaction shown on a character's face or the mood of the setting, which AI video generators render beautifully.

chunks.title: Screenplay & Story Generation — Do It
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Screenplay & Story Generation / Do It.
### Step 1: Define the Production Constraints
Before writing a single word of your script, fill out the project constraints in your brief. Choose:
 Max 1–2 characters to maintain facial consistency.
 Max 2 locations (e.g., a quiet office, a dimly lit street).
 Atmospheric focus: Decide on the visual theme (e.g., neon cyberpunk, dusty retro-future, noir daylight) to anchor prompt styling.
### Step 2: Write the Screenplay with Visual Anchor Prompts
Format your screenplay using a layout that integrates standard screenwriting format with image/video prompt anchors.
 Break the script into individual, discrete shots (each lasting 3-4 seconds).
 For each shot, write a clear visual action description that details the character's facial expression or slow movement.
 Keep dialogue brief (under 15 words per shot) so that TTS models can read it naturally without rushing.
### Step 3: LLM Script Generation
Use a text LLM (like Claude or Gemini) to brainstorm and refine the script. Use a system prompt that forces the AI to respect physical limitations:

chunks.title: Screenplay & Story Generation — Do It
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Screenplay & Story Generation / Do It.
 System Prompt: "You are an AI-first screenwriter. Write a 60-second sci-fi script. Only 1 character. Set entirely in a single room. Avoid any physical object interactions. Focus on facial expressions, slow camera tracking shots, and voiceover dialogue. For every scene, output a detailed visual prompt describing camera movement, framing, character appearance, and lighting."
### Step 4: Prune the Actions
Review the script line by line. If a line says "He stands up, walks to the shelf, grabs a book, opens it, and smiles," prune it. Replace it with: "He sits at the desk, looking at the shelf. [Camera pushes in on his face, showing curiosity]." This is highly renderable.
### Step 5: Save Character & Style Anchors
Create a style sheet with your prompt prefixes (lighting, film stock, aspect ratio) so they can be copy-pasted into every image generator.

chunks.title: Storyboarding & Shot Planning
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Storyboarding & Shot Planning.
# Storyboarding & Shot Planning
 SmartVideo GO AI Academy — Part of the SmartVideo GO AI course library. Everything in this lesson can be produced end-to-end inside SmartVideo GO AI using its Image, Video, Audio, Cinema, Lip-Sync, Storyboard, VFX, Thumbnail and AI Influencer studios, plus the Create-With-AI recipe system.
 A storyboard is the blueprint that stops you from burning credits on random video generations.
Track: AI Filmmaking
Time: ~40 minutes
Prerequisites: Screenplay & Story Generation

chunks.title: Storyboarding & Shot Planning — The Problem
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Storyboarding & Shot Planning / The Problem.
Generating video clips directly from text prompts is a gamble. AI video models are expensive, slow to render, and highly unpredictable. If you type a prompt like "A spaceship interior, John walking towards the door" into a video generator, you might get a great shot, but John’s outfit might be blue, the room might be brightly lit, and the camera angle might be from the ceiling. If you run it again, John's face and clothes will change completely.
If you generate 20 video clips this way, you will end up with a collection of disjointed footage that looks like it belongs to 20 different movies. You will have wasted dozens of dollars in rendering credits and hours of waiting time.
To make a coherent film, you need to establish visual continuity — lighting, color palette, camera framing, and character wardrobe — before you render a single frame of video. Storyboarding is the gatekeeper that locks down these elements at a fraction of the cost.

chunks.title: Storyboarding & Shot Planning — The Concept
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Storyboarding & Shot Planning / The Concept.
Storyboarding for AI filmmaking is the process of generating a sequence of static images that represent the key shots of your film.
By using high-quality image models (like Flux or Midjourney) instead of video models, you can rapidly test style, composition, and consistency. These static storyboard frames then act as the start-frame input for your image-to-video generator.
Visual Style Guide → Character Anchor → Storyboard Images → Image-to-Video
To maintain visual consistency across your storyboard, you rely on a Style Guide containing:
 Style Prefix: A standard set of visual descriptors (film stock, lighting, lens) added to every prompt.
 Aspect Ratio: Fixed layout matching your target screen format.
 Character Reference: A locked-in seed image of your character fed back into the model to maintain facial details.
---

chunks.title: Storyboarding & Shot Planning — Do It
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Storyboarding & Shot Planning / Do It.
### Step 1: Create the Visual Style Guide
Define your aesthetic parameters using the templates/style-guide-template.md. Lock in your film stock (e.g. 35mm film grain), your color palette (e.g. teal shadows, warm amber highlights), and your camera aspect ratio (e.g. --ar 16:9).
### Step 2: Establish the Character Anchor Image
Before drafting scenes, generate your character's "hero portrait."
 Write a detailed prompt describing the character's face, hair, age, and a specific wardrobe element (e.g., "A worn silver flight suit with a red shoulder patch").
 Generate this image using a high-quality model.
 Save the best image. This is your Character Reference Image (Cref).
### Step 3: Generate the Storyboard Frames
For each shot in your screenplay, generate the static frame.
 Start each prompt with your Style Prefix.
 Describe the framing (Wide Shot, Medium Shot, Close-up).
 Reference your Character Anchor Image using the model's image-to-image or character reference capabilities.
 Keep the scene seed constant if the model supports it, varying only the framing and character posture.
### Step 4: Build the Shot List
Log each generated frame into your templates/shot-list-template.md. Note the camera framing, target action, dialogue line, and the file path of the approved static storyboard image.
### Step 5: Check for Visual Continuity

chunks.title: Storyboarding & Shot Planning — Do It
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Storyboarding & Shot Planning / Do It.
Place the storyboard frames next to each other. Do a drift check:
 Does the character’s hair or outfit shift significantly between cuts?
 Does the environment’s lighting change color temperature?
 If yes, re-render the drifting frames, tightening the text prompts to override the changes.
---

Academy lesson: Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts.
# Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts
 SmartVideo GO AI Academy — Part of the SmartVideo GO AI course library. Everything in this lesson can be produced end-to-end inside SmartVideo GO AI using its Image, Video, Audio, Cinema, Lip-Sync, Storyboard, VFX, Thumbnail and AI Influencer studios, plus the Create-With-AI recipe system.
 Camera movement is the difference between an AI slideshow and a movie.
Track: AI Filmmaking
Time: ~50 minutes
Prerequisites: Screenplay & Story Generation, Storyboarding & Shot Planning

chunks.title: Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts — The Problem
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts / The Problem.
Most beginners in AI video generation end up creating what looks like a PowerPoint presentation with slight Ken Burns effects: static characters with wind blowing through their hair, or background dust drifting slightly.
If they try to force camera movements by typing generic text like "the camera moves fast," the video models often glitch, morphing the character's body parts or turning the entire background into a liquid smear.
Real cinema relies on deliberate, structured camera movements — dolly shots, pans, tilts, crane movements, and tracking shots. To make your AI film look premium and deliberate, you need to know how to prompt these movements in a way the video generator's neural network actually understands.

chunks.title: Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts — The Concept
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts / The Concept.
Video models don't think like camera operators; they think in terms of pixel displacement and temporal flow. When you write a movement prompt, you are instructing the model on how pixels should slide across the screen from frame to frame.
To control this displacement effectively, you use three tools:
1. First-Frame Conditioning (Image-to-Video): You feed your storyboard frame from Module 2 as the starting point. This locks the framing and composition.
2. Cinematography Keywords: Using precise industry terms (dolly, pan, tilt) instead of vague action words.
3. Motion Strength Parameters: Adjusting the model's velocity settings to control how much the frame changes over time.
Start Frame (Storyboard) + Camera Direction Prompt + Motion Slider = Cinematic Shot
For advanced shots, you can use First and Last Frame Conditioning, uploading both the starting shot composition and the ending shot composition, forcing the model to generate the transition between them.
---

chunks.title: Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts — Do It
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts / Do It.
### Step 1: Prepare Your Storyboard Start-Frame
Select the static storyboard image you generated in Module 2. Make sure it is at your target aspect ratio (16:9 or 2.39:1). Upload it to your video generator's image-to-video input interface.
### Step 2: Formulate the Motion Prompt
Use the templates/motion-prompt-library.md to choose the camera movement that matches the shot's emotional goal. Add the camera movement phrase to the beginning of your prompt.
 Example: "Slow dolly in, camera slowly pushes toward the astronaut's face, Arri Alexa cinematic style, 24fps."
### Step 3: Set the Motion Strength Slider
If your generator supports it, adjust the motion strength value:
 For dialogue or subtle scenes: Set strength to Low (1–3). This prevents face warping while allowing subtle blinks and head tilts.
 For camera pans, walking, or panning b-roll: Set strength to Medium (4–6).
 For fast action, running, or driving: Set strength to High (7–9).
### Step 4: Render and Review
Render the 4-second clip. Watch the playback and check for:
 The Morphing Zone: Did the background objects bend? Did the character grow extra fingers or change clothes mid-shot?
 Pacing: Is the camera speed jarring or smooth?
 If the shot glitches, lower the motion strength slider and re-render. If it is too static, rewrite the prompt to place the camera direction at the very start of the text.

chunks.title: Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts — Do It
chunks.text:
Academy lesson: Camera Movement & Cinematography Prompts / Do It.
### Step 5: (Optional) Set Last-Frame Conditioning
If the action requires a precise end point, upload a second storyboard image to the Last-Frame Input box. Write a prompt describing the movement between the two images (e.g. "Camera pans left from the cockpit window to focus on the radar screen").
